literal: Flaw will-hide greatness, meanness indeed fault-only having-spoken will-leave.
translation: Greatness hides the flaws of others, but meanness will speak only of their faults.
modern: பெருமைக்குரியவர்கள் மற்றவர்களின் குறைகளை மறைப்பார்கள். ஆனால் சிறுமைக்குணம் கொண்டவர்கள் மற்றவர்களின் குற்றங்களையே கூறிக்கொண்டிருப்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the behavior of the great and the mean-spirited towards others. The word 'aṟṟam' can mean an end or a secret, but here it specifically refers to a vulnerability or a flaw that should be kept private. True greatness chooses to cover and protect the weaknesses of others. In contrast, meanness actively seeks out and broadcasts only the faults of others, as emphasized by the exclusive particle 'ē' in 'kuṟṟamē'.
